_note: TWIST2/HoloMotion raw XRobot -> vita02a (A-sample: serial-ankle legs, 2-DoF neck, wrist chain roll->yaw->pitch). Ported from xrobot_to_vita02.json by scripts/port_vita02_config_to_vita02a.py: same tuning and IK weights; rotation offsets carried over with a rest-pose frame correction (offset := offset * D, D = R_vita02_rest^-1 * R_vita02a_rest per body at qpos0) — identity for base/waist/legs/toes, 1.0 deg for shoulder/elbow frames, ~3.0 deg for the wrist end-effector, whose IK task moved from wrist_yaw_link to wrist_pitch_link (the A-sample wrist EE). The neck_yaw/neck_pitch DoFs have no IK task and ride at 0 via the posture regularizers. Wrist rot offsets were re-solved on 2026-08-05 from three live PICO takes (logs/recordings/pico_vita02a_linkerhand-20260805-180951-take001/002.csv = arms hanging down with palms facing each other and thumbs forward, and forearms horizontal-forward with thumbs up; -191923-take001.csv = arms relaxed, used as the verification pose). The old values were carried over from the old elbow-mounted wrist_task frame and left the hand ~170 deg (left) / ~73 deg (right) from the operator's actual hand orientation, showing up as thumbs pointing inward with the arms down and wrist roll riding near its limit. The defect was shared by the vita02 and vita02a configs alike -- it predates the vita02a vertical-LinkerHand mount work, which is itself exact -- so all five xrobot_to_vita02* configs carry the corrected pair. IMPORTANT, two things the fit must get right: (1) the desired hand orientation has to be expressed in the TORSO frame, not the world frame -- the operator is usually yawed (-25 to -100 deg across these takes) and a world-frame target bakes that yaw into the offset; (2) fitting each side independently breaks left/right symmetry. Correctness check: the wrist L/R convention relation mirror(offL*mountL)^-1 * (offR*mountR) must match the ARM's (the elbow offsets', ~177 deg). It is now 175.8 deg; an earlier independent per-side fit gave 151.7 deg and showed up live as ~30 deg of wrist-yaw and ~40 deg of wrist-roll left/right asymmetry. Residual to the ideal pose is ~8-25 deg, which is the operator's real hand posture rather than fit error. 2026-08-06 follow-up: all six takes recorded after the 08-05 fix showed a consistent +7..+18 deg left+right wrist-yaw SUM (a mirrored pose must sum to ~0) while roll/pitch stayed within noise -- a residual yaw-convention bias the operator saw as the left hand yawed outward with the arms relaxed. Fixed by rotating the LEFT wrist offset 16.6 deg: dR = forearm-relative mirror of the right hand at the 20260806-155124-take001 median pose (model mirror-consistency is exact, 0.00 deg), composed as off_new = off_old * dR (and transported across the vita02/vita02a target-frame relation, exactly the 90-deg mount roll). Predicted yaw sums across all six takes collapse to -0.5..+2.4 deg.
_stream_note: stream_joint_names is the policy wire order (same 28-joint layout as vita02, sim-app profile heldJointStream.wireJointNames): no neck, wrists roll->pitch->yaw. The model tree order differs (neck DoFs, wrist chain roll->yaw->pitch), so sources permute qpos[7:] into this order.

tuning._note: Ported from xrobot_to_vita02.json (originally GMR motion_retarget.py per-robot spec dicts), plus vita02a-specific wrist damping: the A-sample wrist chain is roll->yaw->pitch and its yaw range (-0.913..1.705 left, mirrored right) contains the chain's gimbal singularity at |yaw|~=pi/2 (vita02/g1 chain roll->pitch->yaw only touches it exactly at the +-1.5708 pitch stop), so near full yaw the roll/pitch DoFs go degenerate and the IK dithers between equivalent solutions. prev_posture wrist costs damp that null-space flip inside the solve; the wrist qpos_smoothing group EMAs the remaining solution-branch flips (alpha 0.5 since 2026-09-01, 12.5 ms lag at the ~80 Hz retarget rate; was 0.25 / 37.5 ms). 2026-08-07 waist-yaw tracking fix: the waist_regularizer's group cost (12.0) applied to waist_yaw_joint as well as the hips, and pinned the torso to its default yaw hard enough that the operator's waist twist barely reached the robot -- a round-trip of a PERFECT 45-60 deg twist through the IK returned only 85% of it, and the live takes recorded before the fix show waist_yaw p2p <=2.4 deg (vs +-90 deg of range). The hips/waist_pitch genuinely need the strong pin (the operator's legs are not tracked, so the robot must hold a standing posture), so the cost is overridden per joint rather than lowering the group: joint_costs.waist_yaw_joint = 1.0 restores 100% tracking. Jitter is unchanged (0.377 -> 0.441 deg/frame under 1 deg tracker noise, already EMA'd by the waist qpos_smoothing group (alpha 0.35 then, 0.65 now)), so the pin was buying no stability it was not already getting from the EMA. Costs 0.1-1.0 all track identically; 1.0 keeps a light centering pull in the null space. 2026-09-01 EMA alpha re-tune (lag reduction): the earlier alphas were set against an ASSUMED 1-3 deg tracker noise. Calibrating against 23 real takes in logs/recordings (quietest 100-frame window shows 0.021-0.037 deg/frame wrist jitter surviving the alpha-0.25 EMA) puts real PICO noise at ~0.05-0.1 deg -- roughly 20x lower. At that level mean jitter is invisible (<0.1 deg/frame) for every alpha in 0.25..1.0, and the only thing that scales with alpha is the TAIL: rare (~3-5 per 19 s) IK branch-flip spikes near the wrist singularity, p99.9 ~2.2-2.7 deg/frame but worst-case growing 3.5 (a=0.25) -> 7.0 (0.5) -> 13.9 (unsmoothed) deg/frame. Wrist therefore moved 0.25 -> 0.5 (buys 25 ms for a 3.5 -> 7.0 deg/frame worst case) and NOT further; removing it entirely is what the 13.9 deg/frame snap costs. The waist group has no such tail (p99.9 <= 0.23 deg/frame at alpha 0.65, 0.43 even unsmoothed) and its tracking is alpha-independent (45 deg twist retargets to 44.95 deg at every alpha), so it moved 0.35 -> 0.65 for another 16 ms. Verified identical on the vita02 configs (different wrist chain; waist numbers match to 3 decimals, wrist jitter unaffected at 0.445 deg/frame throughout). Measured kinematically with a calibrated-Gaussian noise model, NOT replayed PICO noise (no raw human-frame captures exist) and with no robot PD loop in the path -- re-check on hardware before lowering alpha further.

groups._note: Legs were unsmoothed while the wrists were not, even though both chains sit near a singularity: a straight knee is the leg's, and the IK branch flips there show up as per-frame spikes in the reference the tracking policy follows. Lighter than the wrist EMA on purpose — leg lag costs balance, so this only clips the tail. Re-tune with scripts/sweep_qpos_smoothing_alpha.py against a real take rather than by feel.

input_pose_correction._note: PICO wrist-tracking asymmetry compensation (2026-08-07). With both forearms horizontal-forward the tracked LEFT wrist is rotated ~26 deg away from the mirror of the right (stable across sessions/donnings: 23.9/25.6/26.0 deg about the same hand-frame axis over three takes on two days), while arms-down the same measure is ~0 -- pose-dependent, so folding it into the constant wrist rot_offset would trade the error 1:1 into the arms-down pose. Instead the correction is right-multiplied onto the tracked Left_Wrist orientation itself and blended by forearm elevation: identity with the arm hanging (elevation <= zero_below_deg), full at horizontal-forward (>= full_above_deg). Solved from pico_vita02a_linkerhand-20260807-162956-take001 (median pose; the operator confirmed the RIGHT hand as correct, so the left is corrected onto the mirror of the right): dR = TL^T M TR M with TL/TR the elbow-relative achieved EE rotations and M = diag(1,-1,1), expressed in the human Left_Wrist frame as rotvec = log(offL dR offL^T). Human-input-side, therefore the SAME values are correct for every robot config.

velocity_limit._note: Caps how far one solve may move a joint. The units are awkward — solve_ik runs at model.opt.timestep, up to max_iter+1 times per frame — so the old hardcoded 3*pi was ~12 deg/frame and constrained nothing. These values are chosen to bound a branch flip, not to shape motion.
